role: Runtime hallucination guard for the AI coach: regex-scans a drafted reply for 'current value' claims (live HR/power/alpha1/HR drift; TSB/ATL/CTL/ACWR; overnight RMSSD/recovery score; last night's sleep duration/efficiency), compares against live snapshot or app state, returns span-precise Discrepancies plus corrected text, and buffers corrections for the next turn's system prompt.
types: MetricsVerifier: enum — namespace of pure claim checks
MetricsVerifier.Discrepancy: struct — metric/claimed/actual/delta/range of one wrong claim
MetricsVerifier.SpelledRewrite: struct (private) — original vs normalized NSRange of one spelled-number rewrite
state: mem:MetricsVerifier.pendingCorrections (OSAllocatedUnfairLock<[Discrepancy]>, process-local, max 4, cleared on consume)
static let generalSleepMarkers / otherNightMarkers / timeMarkers / targetMarkers (sentence-filter regexes)
static let onesAndTeens / tens (word->int maps for spelled numbers)
toplevel: Static regex constants and word maps (lines 352-356, 444-450, 535-541, 639-649); the pendingCorrections lock (582). All patterns are compiled lazily through DebugLogger.compiledPattern which caches and NSLogs compile failures.

flags.text: Voice mode: the voice overlay tells the model to say numbers like a person ('one-sixty') and base rule 1 gives 'Your HR is 150' (no unit) as the model format, but verify() runs on raw text (no spelled-number normalisation, and the normaliser only covers 0-99) and every live pattern requires digits plus 'bpm'/'W'. Spoken live HR/power fabrications pass the guard unchecked.

The TSB/ATL/CTL/ACWR patterns require the number immediately after the abbreviation (`\bTSB\s+<number>`), but the system prompt instructs the model to phrase it 'TSB is -8.8'; 'TSB is', 'TSB of', 'TSB at', 'TSB: ' are never checked, so the guard misses the very phrasing the prompt asks for.

Recovery score is verified against the newest RELIABLE overnight of any date, while the prompt's recovery_score_today uses DeterministicIntent.todaysOvernightEntry (night whose midpoint is today). When there is no reliable night today the verifier 'corrects' recovery claims to an older night's score the model was never given.

Sleep source of truth is the newest overnight that HAS a frozen sleepSnapshot (no date bound, no check that it is last night). get_sleep 'latest' answers an un-accepted newest night from a live HealthKit read when its snapshot is nil, so the model quotes last night's real duration and the verifier rewrites it (chat turn is saved rewritten; voice is spoken rewritten) to an OLDER night's duration/efficiency.

units.does: Live HR claim check: when the snapshot has heartRate, matches 'your (current|live) HR/heart rate is ... N bpm' / 'HR right now N bpm' and returns discrepancies off by >5 bpm, formatted 'N bpm'.

branches.effect: returns [] (HR not checked); otherwise runs claimsMatching with tolerance 5

units.does: Live power claim check: when snapshot.powerWatts exists, matches 'your power/wattage is N W/watts' / 'power right now N W', tolerance 15 W, formatted 'N W'.
Live DFA alpha1 claim check: when snapshot.alpha1 exists, matches 'your (DFA) α1/alpha1 is X.YY' (decimal required), tolerance 0.10, formatted %.2f.
Live HR-drift claim check: when snapshot.liveHRDriftPercent exists, matches 'your (HR) drift is N%' / 'drift right now N%', tolerance 1.5 points, formatted %.1f%%.
Public entry for live-workout claims: returns HR + power + alpha1 + drift discrepancies against the WorkoutAIContext snapshot (ranges index the raw input text; no spelled-number normalisation).

branches.effect: returns [] (no live workout => nothing verified); else concatenates the four checks

flags.text: Live-workout claim checking (HR/power/alpha1/drift) runs only on the voice path; the typed-chat pipeline only calls verifyAppStateClaims, so a typed 'your HR is 142 bpm' fabrication during a workout is saved and shown unchecked, although the module header presents this as the runtime backstop for live-snapshot contradictions.

units.does: Public entry for app-state claims (MainActor): normalises spelled numbers, runs training-load, overnight and last-night-sleep checks on the normalised text, maps each range back to the original text (dropping any that fail to map) and returns them with correctedText (original with only the claimed spans replaced, nil if none).

flags.text: remap returns nil when the mapped NSRange cannot convert to a String range and compactMap drops that discrepancy silently: a detected wrong number is neither corrected nor logged.

Every call (each spoken voice chunk via speak(), each finished chat turn) synchronously decrypts and JSON-decodes archived overnight session files on the MainActor in latestReliableOvernight and latestOvernightSleep, even when the text contains no RMSSD/recovery/sleep claim; latestReliableOvernight checks reliability only after decoding although SessionArchiveEntry.isReliableForHRVAggregates could filter before any file I/O.

units.does: Training-load check: reads TrainingLoadRegistry.live(); matches 'TSB [negative ]N' (negates spelled 'negative'), 'ATL N', 'CTL N' (each with a lookahead refusing durations/percent) with tolerances 2/3/3, then ACWR; formats TSB %+.1f, ATL/CTL %.1f.

branches.effect: returns [] — no load claim verified; otherwise runs TSB/ATL/CTL/ACWR checks

flags.text: Does not consult TrainingLoadVisibility.isPaused: while training load is paused the prompt omits the load numbers (trainingLoadSections) yet any TSB/ATL/CTL claim is still rewritten to the registry value.

units.does: ACWR check: when the registry ACWR is non-nil, matches 'ACWR N' with tolerance 0.15, formatted %.2f.
Overnight check: takes the latest reliable overnight session; if it has analysisResult RMSSD, checks 'RMSSD [of] N [ms]' with tolerance 8 ms; if it has recoveryScore, runs recoveryScoreClaims.

branches.effect: adds RMSSD discrepancies (tolerance 8.0, '%.0f ms'); when nil (no session or no analysis) RMSSD is not checked
adds recoveryScoreClaims; else recovery not checked

flags.text: RMSSD and recovery patterns need the number directly after the label ('RMSSD [of] N', 'recovery N'); 'RMSSD is 48', 'your recovery score is 72', 'recovery score of 72' are never checked, so the common phrasings of the two overnight metrics pass the guard unverified.

units.does: Returns the newest overnight archive entry (by entry date, any age) whose lightweight-decoded session has analysisResult or recoveryScore and isReliableForHRVAggregates (not .insufficient/.preSleep); retrieval failures are logged and skipped.

Recovery claim check: matches 'recovery N' (not followed by a duration/percent), compares to score10*10 with tolerance 4 (0-100 scale), then passes each hit through onTheClaimsScale to accept/correct 0-10-scale claims.

branches.cond: actual value is a whole number

flags.text: The 0-100 correction value is score10*10 unrounded and unclamped, formatted '%.1f' when fractional (e.g. '84.6'), while the dashboard and the prompt's recovery_score_today use RecoveryScoreCalculator.displayScore (rounded, clamped: 85); a corrected reply states a recovery number the user never sees on screen.

units.does: Post-filter for recovery discrepancies: drops a claim within 1.0 of the 0-10 score; keeps claims >10 as 0-100 discrepancies; re-expresses claims <=10 as 0-10 corrections (actual formatted 0-10, delta on 0-10 scale).

branches.cond: d.claimed does not parse as Double
branches.effect: returns d unchanged (claimed is formatter output so it always parses)
returns nil — treated as the same score on the 0-10 scale
returns d (0-100 discrepancy already outside tolerance 4)
actual10 formatted %.0f else %.1f; returns a new Discrepancy on the 0-10 scale

units.does: Last-night sleep check: reads the newest overnight with sleep and runs sleepDiscrepancies with its nightSleepMinutes and measuredSleepEfficiency.

branches.cond: no overnight with a sleepSnapshot of >0 minutes

flags.text: Sleep source of truth is the newest overnight that HAS a frozen sleepSnapshot (no date bound, no check that it is last night). get_sleep 'latest' answers an un-accepted newest night from a live HealthKit read when its snapshot is nil, so the model quotes last night's real duration and the verifier rewrites it (chat turn is saved rewritten; voice is spoken rewritten) to an OLDER night's duration/efficiency.

units.does: Returns the sleepSnapshot of the newest overnight entry (any age, no reliability or date check) whose lightweight session has a snapshot with nightSleepMinutes > 0.

Sleep claims: duration discrepancies plus (when efficiency known) efficiency discrepancies, then keeps only those whose sentence is not a norm/advice/other-night sentence and that do not overlap an already kept one.

branches.effect: adds efficiency discrepancies; else efficiency not checked

branches.cond: discrepancy sentence is about another night/norm OR overlaps an earlier kept discrepancy

units.does: Runs the three sleep-duration regexes (case-insensitive) over the text and turns each match into a Discrepancy via durationDiscrepancy; a pattern that fails to compile is skipped (logged by compiledPattern).

One sleep-duration match -> Discrepancy when the claim parses, its sentence is about now, and it differs from nightMinutes by >5 min (precise claim) or >30 min (whole hours); renders claimed/actual in long ('hours') or short ('h') form matching the claim.

branches.cond: claim group missing OR hours unparseable OR sentence has time/target markers OR range conversion fails

branches.effect: returns nil (within tolerance); else builds Discrepancy

units.does: Parses the hours (decimal allowed) and optional minutes groups into total minutes and whether the claim is finer than a whole hour.

branches.effect: minutes 0; present but unparseable -> 0 (?? 0); isPrecise = minutes present or hours has '.'

units.does: Formats minutes as '6h 55m'/'7h' (short) or '6 hours and 55 minutes'/'1 hour and 1 minute'/'7 hours' (long).

branches.effect: ' and 1 minute' else ' and N minutes'

units.does: Sleep-efficiency claims ('sleep efficiency of 95%', '95% sleep efficiency', '95% efficient') with tolerance 1 point, kept only when the sentence mentions sleep/slept/asleep.
True when the sentence containing the range matches sleep|slept|asleep.

True when the sentence containing the range matches general sleep-norm markers (need, recommend, adults, per night, ranges 'N-N', 'to N') or other-night markers (month/weekday names, 'nights', 'weeks', dates).
Finds the Foundation sentence holding the range and returns whether the case-insensitive pattern matches inside it; a pattern that fails to compile yields false.
Returns text with each discrepancy's range replaced by its actual value, applied back-to-front, skipping ranges outside the current bounds; nil when there are no discrepancies.

flags.text: Ranges index the ORIGINAL string and are applied to a mutated copy; correct only because replacements go back-to-front and ranges never overlap. Two overlapping discrepancies from different metric checks (no cross-metric overlap filter in verifyAppStateClaims) would splice with stale indices.

units.does: Generic matcher: compiles the pattern (cached, case-insensitive), maps every match through discrepancy(from:); a compile failure returns [] after compiledPattern NSLogs it.

branches.effect: returns [] (the comment at 33-43 says failures are logged, but the metric is then unchecked); else maps matches

units.does: Turns one match into a Discrepancy: requires value+claim groups, a parseable value and a 'current value' sentence; negates spelled 'negative N' when allowed; returns nil within tolerance.

branches.cond: value/claim group missing, value not a Double, or sentence is past/target/comparison
delta <= tolerance or range conversion fails
branches.effect: returns nil; else Discrepancy with formatter-rendered claimed/actual

units.does: False when the sentence containing the match has any time marker (ago, yesterday, last week, earlier, before...) or target/comparison marker (average, keep, if, should, under, over, than, higher...).

flags.text: The marker lists are broad (if, would, could, should, over, under, than, before, earlier, yesterday...). Any sentence containing one is not verified, including the base prompt's own example headline 'Recovery 72, slightly down from 76 yesterday' — the guard fails open on the comparison phrasing the prompt asks the model to lead with.

units.does: Returns the Foundation .bySentences range that contains range.location, unioned with the range; falls back to the range itself.

branches.effect: continue enumerating; when found, union + stop

units.does: Formats discrepancies as one '[Hallucination guard] metric=claimed:X actual:Y Δd | ...' log line; '' when empty.
Appends discrepancies to the process-local pending-corrections buffer under the lock, skipping ones already pending with the same metric/claimed/actual, then keeps only the newest 4.

branches.cond: an identical metric+claimed+actual is already pending

units.does: Atomically takes and clears the pending corrections; returns nil when none, else a '# Last turn correction — DO NOT FABRICATE' block with a tool-use instruction and one bullet per correction.

branches.effect: appends '• You said metric=claimed — actual was actual.'

flags.text: The buffer is consumed when the prompt is COMPOSED, not when a send succeeds. The fallback path re-composes the prompt for the next provider after a failure (AssistantViewModel+Tools fallbackSystemPrompt), and tests calling composeSplit also drain it, so the one-shot reminder is lost whenever the first attempt fails.

units.does: Public wrapper returning only the normalised text (spelled numbers to digits).

Rewrites each spelled-number match ('negative thirty-one point seven' -> '-31.7') into digits, recording original/normalized ranges for every rewrite; returns the input unchanged with no rewrites if the pattern does not compile.

flags.text: Every spelled 0-99 word in the reply is rewritten (e.g. 'one' -> '1') before matching, and 'point' consumes only one digit word ('point seven five' -> '.7 5'); only 0-99 is handled, so a spoken HR like 'one hundred forty' is never normalised.

units.does: Moves a discrepancy's range from normalized to original text via originalOffset for start (snap to start) and end (snap to end); nil if the resulting NSRange does not convert.

branches.cond: mapped NSRange not convertible to a Range in the original

units.does: Maps a normalized-text UTF-16 offset to the original: accumulates shift from rewrites ending before it; an offset strictly inside a rewrite snaps to the rewrite's original start or end.

branches.cond: offset inside the rewrite (after its start)

units.does: Builds the spelled-number regex string from onesAndTeens (longest first), tens and single digit words: optional 'negative', ones/teen OR tens[-ones], optional 'point <digit>'.
Converts one spelled-number match to a digit string: integer part, optional '.d' from the point group, '-' prefix when 'negative' matched.

branches.effect: ?? 0 fallback (cannot happen: pattern only admits listed words)

units.does: Integer part of a spelled number: a ones/teens word on its own, or a tens word plus optional ones suffix.

branches.effect: adds it; else returns tens value
